keyVerseText: And the whole valley of the dead bodies, and of the ashes, and all the fields unto the brook of Kidron, unto the corner of the horse gate toward the east, shall be holy unto the LORD; it shall not be plucked up, nor thrown down any more for ever.
rootMeaning: The Hebrew noun שְׁרֵמָה (shᵉrêmâh) likely originates as an orthographical variant of שְׁדֵמָה (shᵉdêmâh), which denotes a cultivated field or a blasted field. This root highlights the concept of land prepared or left fallow, emphasizing the physical and agricultural reality of a field rather than a generic open space. Understanding this root enriches the simple English term "field" by connecting it to notions of cultivation, barrenness, and the land's condition in relation to human stewardship.
usageInScripture: This word appears only once in Scripture, specifically in Jeremiah 31:40, where it is used to describe portions of land that will be consecrated to the LORD. Its singular occurrence suggests a specialized or contextually significant use rather than a broad lexical range. Although no top translations are listed, the consistent rendering as "field" or related terms underscores its straightforward meaning as a tract of land, reinforcing the tangible, physical dimension of sacred space in the biblical narrative.
theologicalSignificance: The concept of שְׁרֵמָה as a field, especially one set apart in Jeremiah 31:40, speaks profoundly to God's intention for His creation. Fields represent places of provision, labor, and blessing, but also vulnerability to destruction or neglect. That this field is described as holy and permanently preserved reflects God's sovereign care and the promise of restoration. For the Christian faith, this underscores the truth that God redeems not only individuals but also the created order, securing a place of peace and sanctity that points forward to the new heavens and new earth. It reminds believers that God's covenant includes the physical realm, inviting them to trust in His eternal purposes.
keyVerseReflection: Jeremiah 31:40 declares that all the fields, including the valley of dead bodies and ashes, will be made holy to the LORD and will never again be destroyed or uprooted. The word שְׁרֵמָה here emphasizes the tangible land that God will preserve as sacred, signifying a profound transformation from desolation to divine protection. This highlights God's promise of restoration and permanence, assuring that what was once vulnerable will be secured forever in His holy presence.
